question: why do six of the sixteen pinned models carry no campaign measurement?
method: each model was driven through the study pipeline to the stage that stops it
finding: one of the four was not a defect at all. QDQ failed because the reference was computed on a different numerical path; INT8 fails because the lowering implements a different arithmetic from the operator specification; the two dynamic-shape models need a missing capability.

tiny-yolov3-11.root_cause: the spatial dims of this model's input are declared with no name at all, [N, 3, <empty>, <empty>], so no dimension parameter exists to bind. nn.conv2d needs static extents to expand its loop nest, so the call survives into c.prepare. The graph reads its own spatial extent from a second input tensor, which is a real property of the model.
tiny-yolov3-11.fix_scope: a shape entry on the ONNX frontend, so a caller can declare the concrete input shape when the graph declares none. This is the same requirement TVM and ONNX-MLIR place on their users, so supplying it is parity rather than a special case.

fixed: opt.signature declares the input shape the graph does not name, so the entry becomes tensor<f32,[1,3,416,416]> and the convolutions come out static.
Resize now computes its extent from literal scales: [1,128,13,13] with scales [1,1,2,2] types as tensor<f32,[1,128,26,26], which matches the model's own initialiser.
progress.next_blocker: c.prepare stops on operator * in main with an unknown-typed left operand and an int right, which is a stride computation over a shape vector. Seventy-three tensors in the converted graph still carry a dynamic extent, twenty-eight of them tensor<i32,[_]> shape vectors: this model computes its own extents at run time from a second input tensor, so declaring the input shape is not enough.
progress.note: each fixed layer exposes the next, which is what adding a model to a compiler looks like; the two fixes are general capabilities rather than anything about this model.
progress.next_capability: letting a caller supply the value of a shape-carrying input and constant-folding it, which would make those seventy-three tensors static. That is a real feature rather than a special case, and it is a further layer beyond opt.signature.

blocker_chain.step_1: declared input extents have no dimension parameter; opt.signature fixes that and the entry becomes tensor<f32,[1,3,416,416]> (done)
blocker_chain.step_2: Resize is given scales rather than sizes, so its extent now follows from floor(input * scale) computed in integers (done)
blocker_chain.step_3: the graph still reads its own spatial extent from a second input tensor, image_shape, which the ONNX file declares as a real input and not an initialiser, so seventy-three tensors keep a dynamic extent
blocker_chain.step_4: c.prepare then inlines a quantisation helper whose body computes a per-channel stride as stride *= S[dim], and S[dim] is one of those dynamic extents, so the multiply reaches the C backend with an unknown-typed operand and is refused

what_a_fix_needs.compiler: a way for a caller to bind an input to a constant, so image_shape's uses are replaced by a literal and the shape arithmetic folds. opt.signature covers types; this would cover values.
what_a_fix_needs.study: the ONNX reference generator and the study subject both assume a single input, so a two-input model needs the shape tensor fed consistently on both sides.
what_a_fix_needs.cost: unlike SSD this graph is small, 1,146 operations against mnist-8's 1,108 at 1.2 s, so the iteration cost here is seconds rather than tens of minutes. The work is the feature and the plumbing, not a performance wall.

bind_attempt.what_was_built: opt.bind, which replaces a parameter's uses with a constant, the value-level counterpart of opt.signature; the parameter stays in the signature so a caller still feeds it. It also needed floating-point constant construction at compile time, which the evaluator lacked: Attr already carried a real, so f32 and f64 joined int in the fundamental set and were declared in the base module.
bind_attempt.what_it_did: binding image_shape to [416, 416] before conversion removed the unknown-typed multiply that stopped preparation. The graph then stopped on an uneliminated onnx.model instead: inserting the constant's construction into the entry keeps the conversion from consuming the model op, and binding after conversion does not help because shape inference has already run.
bind_attempt.why_it_is_not_landed: with the feature in place eight tests fail, and the module changes depend on the evaluator change, so it is a partial feature rather than a fix. It is reverted: the tree is at the state that passes 68 of 68 with every target built.
bind_attempt.next_step: make the conversion tolerate the model op not being first, or place the constant without adding ops to the entry, then land the whole thing together with the tests green.

state_after_round_26.what_was_found: the model op is blocked by onnx.Squeeze -- the node that consumes image_shape. With the input bound to a constant the conversion no longer converts that node, and the frontend tag it keeps alive is what stops the model op being erased.
state_after_round_26.why: squeeze_result computes the node's result type from its input's type, and the constant opt.bind builds arrives as tensor<f32,_> -- unranked -- because tensor.tensor is generic in its shape and does not adopt the result type the call was given. No type means the rule refuses, the node is stranded, and the conversion never finishes.
state_after_round_26.tried: stating the result type on the call and again on the value after each step, and letting the reshape rule adopt a computed type when the declared one is unknown. The type still arrives unranked, so the remaining work is in how a constructed constant's type is established rather than in the conversion rules.
state_after_round_26.kept: the reshape rule now adopts the type it computed when the declared type is unknown instead of refusing, which is a general robustness fix; the suite is green at 68/68 with it.

ssd-mobilenetv1-12.outcome: no longer rejected; preparation does not finish in a practical time
ssd-mobilenetv1-12.message: opt.fold branch type mismatch: tensor<f32, [_, _]> and tensor<f32, _>
ssd-mobilenetv1-12.root_cause: a rank-precision gap, now fixed. A branch result was not folded when the value reaching it carried a tensor whose dimension argument is not a list -- a tensor of unknown rank -- while the branch declared a ranked one. opt.fold refined a value only when its type was the fully unknown '_'. The predicate matters: tensor.valid requires the dimension argument to be a list, so tensor<f32,_> is not a valid tensor type and a guard written with tensor.valid never matches it.
ssd-mobilenetv1-12.fix: opt.fold now refines a tensor whose dimension argument is not a list to the rank its branch declares. Committed; the suite is green at 68/68. An earlier attempt at the same rule was reverted after five tests failed, and that revert was wrong: the failures were a missing dependency, because the rule used tensor.valid, which needs the tensor module in scope and opt did not use it. The rule now needs only base accessors.
ssd-mobilenetv1-12.new_blocker: with the fold error gone the preparation runs for over fifty minutes without finishing, against 1.2 s for mnist-8, 11.9 s for squeezenet1.1-7 and 43.6 s for UltraFace. The obstruction is therefore cost rather than correctness, the same class as XCiT's timeout, and it is a pass over a graph that carries the detection postprocessor's while loops.

new_frontier.where: after the best-effort batch change the preparation completes its passes in 35 s and stops on 'c: unsupported call remains: tensor.cast' -- a place this model has never reached before.
new_frontier.the_call: the first one casts the entry tensor from tensor<u8,[1,320,320,3]> to tensor<f32,[1,320,320,3]>. It carries no op metadata and its callee has a body, so the exposure conditions for inlining it are all met and the inline itself is what fails.
what_it_is_not: the element pair: a minimal function casting u8 to f32 prepares in 0.09 s
the shape: the same minimal function prepares in 0.09 s at [4], [1,32,32,3] and [1,320,320,3]
the frontend tag: the call reports meta=0
the expression-region rule that refuses stateful bodies in a branch output, since the call sits at the top level of main
new_frontier.what_is_established: no other model in the campaign contains a tensor.cast at all -- UltraFace, MNIST and SqueezeNet have zero before and zero after preparation -- so this path has never been exercised by anything measured, and there is no working example to compare against.
new_frontier.next_step: find what differs between the minimal function that works and this call in place: the candidates are its consumers, since the cast feeds tensor.shape, and the state of the module when the round reaches it. The iteration cost is 35 s, so this is now a cheap question; before the batch change it could not be asked at all.

minimal_reproduction.cost: 0.1 s, against 35 s for the model
minimal_reproduction.trigger: a tensor.cast whose result is used more than once. Returning the cast prepares, binding it and returning it prepares, and returning f + f or casting it again fails.
minimal_reproduction.symptom: preparation stops on 'c: unsupported call remains: _' -- the stranded call has an empty callee name, which is a different symptom from the model's, where the name was tensor.cast. Something in the expansion is producing a call that no longer resolves, and the model's first operation is the same shape of thing: one cast of the entry tensor, consumed by tensor.shape and by everything downstream.
minimal_reproduction.why_it_matters: this reduces the question from a 19,432-operation graph that takes 35 s per attempt to six lines that take a tenth of a second, and it is the first reproduction of this failure that does not need the model at all.

trigger_narrowed.statement: a tensor.cast whose result is consumed by another operation. The cast alone prepares, the consumer alone prepares, and the two together leave a live call in main with an empty callee name that resolves to nothing, which preparation then stops on.
trigger_narrowed.reading: it is not the number of uses and not the cast on its own: it is one inlinable call whose result feeds another inlinable call. The cast's body is a loop over numel and so are the bodies of the operations that consume it, so the failure is in how the expander handles a call consumed by a call rather than in either one alone.
trigger_narrowed.symptom: the stranded operation is live, sits in main, takes one argument and produces one result, and has an empty callee name -- something the expander produced no longer resolves.

origin.symptom_read_carefully: the stranded operation takes one argument and produces one result and its callee prints as '_', which is the name of the unknown type rather than an empty string. It is a conversion to a type that was never instantiated, which is the shape of the body of tensor.cast itself: out[i] = B(x[i]), where B is the element type parameter.
origin.ruled_out: the semantic name passed into Env::expand is not empty. A probe on the path that builds it, which would produce an empty name if the call's target failed to resolve, never fired, so every call resolved and the unnamed operation is not a call whose name was lost on the way in.
origin.established: the operation does not exist before exposure -- opt.basic leaves none -- so the expander creates it while inlining a call whose result another call consumes.
origin.leading_explanation: instantiating tensor.cast for this pair of element types leaves the conversion in its body pointing at an uninstantiated type parameter, and the resulting operation is not a call to anything. Returning the cast directly does not exercise that path; handing its result to another operation does.
origin.next_step: watch what Mod::expand creates when the callee's body contains a conversion to a type parameter, and compare the two variants at that point rather than at the symptom.

root_cause.statement: a generic parameter that appears only in the return type is not inferred at a call whose result is bound to a variable. tensor.cast has that shape: B is the target element type and appears nowhere in the parameters, so the call needs the expected type to get it.
root_cause.evidence: a probe on the substitution that runs while a callee's body is copied into the call site prints callee='B' valid=1 bindings=2 -> '_' beside callee='E' valid=1 bindings=2 -> 'f32': the same substitution resolves another function's parameter and leaves this one unknown.
root_cause.why_binding_matters: returning the call directly supplies the expected type and prepares; binding it to a variable does not, and annotating the binding explicitly does not either, so the expectation is not reaching the call's generic inference through the annotation.
root_cause.consequence: inlining then copies the body with B still in it, the conversion B(x[i]) becomes a call named after the type parameter, and preparation stops on it.

where_a_fix_belongs.corrected: the annotation does reach the call. Probing the result types that Mod::expand collects shows 'mine' arriving as tensor<_, [4]> without an annotation and tensor<f32, [4]> with one, so a let's declared type is already carried into the call's own output type.
where_a_fix_belongs.so_the_fix_is_not_in_the_frontend: expected_returns is correct and resolve_overload still does not bind the parameter from it. The parameter appears only in the return type, and the resolver does not use the expectation to bind it, so the generic comes back unknown and the substitution in the inlined body leaves the parameter in place.
where_a_fix_belongs.fix: bind a return-only type parameter from the expected return type inside resolve_overload, which is where the expectation is already available and already ignored.

exact_site.file: src/verify.cpp, the expected-returns loop at 391-402, inside the overload matcher declared at src/detail.h:128
exact_site.what_it_does: for each candidate return it skips expectations that are unknown and otherwise unifies the candidate's return against the expected one, keeping the bindings. For this call that is tensor<B, S> against tensor<f32, [4]>, which should bind B to f32.
exact_site.observed: it does not. Mod::expand receives tensor<f32, [4]> as the expectation for the annotated case and the generic still comes back unknown, so the failure is inside this matcher rather than upstream of it.
exact_site.next_step: instrument inside the loop: whether it is reached for this call, whether unify returns true, and what the bindings hold afterwards. The reproduction takes a tenth of a second, so this is cheap.

measured_inside.the_loop_is_reached: yes, and with the right expectation: the probe prints formal='tensor<B, S>' expected='tensor<f32, [4]>'.
measured_inside.unify_succeeds: unify('tensor<B, S>','tensor<f32, [4]>') = 1, and it leaves two bindings where one was held before, so both B and S are bound inside the matcher.
measured_inside.so_the_loss_is_after_the_matcher: the bindings are correct inside the expected-returns loop and the generic still reaches Mod::expand as unknown, so what is lost is between this loop and the caller's generics out-parameter.
measured_inside.next_step: read how resolve_overload fills its generics out-parameter from the bindings the matcher produced -- whether it copies them, whether a later candidate resets them, or whether it fills the out-parameter from a different set.

efficientnet-lite4-11-qdq.message: 1139.371 ms to 350.123 ms, 3.25x, ONNX Runtime 43.342 ms on the same reference
efficientnet-lite4-11-qdq.meaning: the earlier failure was the reference, not the compiler: ONNX Runtime's default optimisation rewrites DequantizeLinear->Conv->QuantizeLinear into an integer kernel, a different path from the QDQ graph the compiler implements. Joggle matches the graph as written to 7.5e-9.

efficientnet-lite4-11-int8.message: max_abs_error 4.344e-03 over 123 elements after the int32 accumulation fix

standard.note: ai.onnx operators with a specified int32 accumulation

runtime_private.note: com.microsoft contrib operators, numerically defined by the runtime's own kernels

efficientnet-lite4-11-int8.meaning: 92 of the 93 quantised operators are standard and now accumulate in int32 as specified; that moved the error only from 4.462e-3 to 4.344e-3, so the accumulation arithmetic is not the dominant term. The remaining 25 instances are ONNX Runtime contrib operators whose documented formula is itself a float expression, which is what the lowering implements, while ONNX Runtime evaluates them with fixed-point kernels. The residual is therefore the distance between two implementations of runtime-private operators rather than a standard-conformance failure, which is why this is not pursued further: each iteration costs about ten minutes in c.prepare alone.
efficientnet-lite4-11-int8.cost_note: the model's preparation runs the interpreted compiler over 91 convolutions and takes about 600 s, so one correctness iteration is roughly fifteen minutes.

tflite-mobilenetv2.meaning: executes, but was timed against LiteRT by its own frontend study rather than in this campaign

root_causes.shared: Two of the four rejections are the same capability gap, not two bugs: the compiler has no support for shapes that are not static. TinyYOLOv3 declares a variable-size input and reads its own spatial extent from a second input tensor, so its convolutions carry '_' spatial dims and cannot be expanded; SSD-MobileNetV1 has free entry dims and a while loop whose carried tensors differ in rank.

tiny-yolov3-11.evidence: the entry reads fn main<N: int>(input_1: tensor<f32,[N,3,_,_]>, image_shape: tensor<f32,[N,2]>)
tiny-yolov3-11.cause: the graph's spatial extent is data-dependent, so nn.conv2d's loop bounds are unknown and the call survives into c.prepare
tiny-yolov3-11.fix_scope: shape-input constant folding plus dynamic extents through the specializer and the C backend

ssd-mobilenetv1-12.evidence: the entry carries free dims unk__6578 and a loop_scan tensor typed [_,_]
ssd-mobilenetv1-12.cause: static-control folding will not fold a branch whose arms carry tensor<f32,[_,_]> and tensor<f32,_>; the two differ in rank
ssd-mobilenetv1-12.fix_scope: rank unification for dynamically ranked values, plus dynamic extents

efficientnet-lite4-11-qdq.cause: the artifact executes and misses the stored reference in the shared quantised path
efficientnet-lite4-11-qdq.fix_scope: numerical: this is the one of the four that looks like a defect rather than a missing feature

xcit-tiny-12-p8-224-opset17.cause: preparation cost exceeds its recorded timeout

assessment.eleven_of_sixteen: EfficientNet-Lite4 QDQ measures at 3.25x; the other ten campaign models are unchanged.

remaining.tiny-yolov3-11: advanced from conv2d to a data-dependent shape path; needs shape-value folding
remaining.ssd-mobilenetv1-12: rank precision at a branch, and the fix belongs with the exposure mechanism
remaining.efficientnet-lite4-11-int8: 92 of 93 operators are standard and now conform; the residual is two runtime-private contrib operators

assessment.note: each attempt is recorded with its outcome, including the two that were reverted for breaking tests. No model was made to pass by special-casing it.
